recent_posts.title: Proposal: Auto-generate Block Editor Handbook docs from block.json
recent_posts.summary: A proposal to auto-generate Block Editor Handbook documentation from each core block's block.json file. The pipeline would create per-block API reference pages at build time, keeping docs in sync with the codebase automatically. Generated content lives in README.md files next to block source code, using token delimiters to preserve hand-written narrative alongside auto-generated API reference. The initial PR was merged then reverted due to insufficient community discussion, and this post opens a formal feedback period running through May 25th with a Hallway Hangout on May 18th.

recent_posts.title: WordPress 7.0 real-time collaboration testing needed from web hosts by May 4th
recent_posts.summary: WordPress Core is requesting web hosts and database admins to test the Real Time Collaboration (RTC) feature planned for WordPress 7.0 by May 4th. A test suite requiring only bash, cURL, WP-CLI, and patch has been provided. Hosts are asked to run tests against their actual production configurations (not fresh installs) and submit results to WordPress.org using a bot account. Results will be aggregated and analyzed by hosting type to inform architectural decisions before the 7.0 release. The RTC feature is part of the Phase 3 roadmap and opens the door to agentic collaborators and future features like suggestion mode.

recent_posts.title: Presence API Feature Plugin
recent_posts.summary: A new experimental WordPress feature plugin called the Presence API adds a system-wide awareness layer to the WordPress admin, showing who is logged in, which admin screens they are on, and which posts they are actively editing. It introduces dashboard widgets ('Who's Online' and 'Active Posts'), an admin bar online indicator with avatar stacks, a post list 'Editors' column, a Users list 'Online' filter, REST endpoints, WP-CLI commands, and a post-lock bridge. Data is stored in a dedicated ephemeral table with a 60-second TTL and flows through the existing Heartbeat API. The plugin can be tested in WordPress Playground with 5- or 40-user blueprints. It is experimental and community feedback is being solicited.

recent_posts.title: Roster of design tools per block (WordPress 7.0 edition)
recent_posts.summary: A reference lookup table listing all core WordPress blocks and the design tools each supports, updated for WordPress 7.0. Covers features like typography, color, dimension, border, layout, gradient, duotone, shadow, and background image. Notable changes include the Verse block being renamed to Poetry, several new blocks added (Accordion, Breadcrumbs, Icon, Math, Post Time to Read, Term Query), and the removal of the Pattern Overrides/Block Bindings column due to architectural changes in 6.9 and 7.0 that made per-block opt-in support too granular for a simple table.

recent_posts.title: What’s new in Gutenberg 23.0? (22 April)
recent_posts.summary: Gutenberg 23.0 has been released with 174 merged PRs. Key highlights include an experimental revisions panel for templates, template parts, and patterns; Site Title and Site Tagline fields added to the Design › Identity panel in the Site Editor; and real-time collaboration (RTC) improvements including legacy meta box compatibility via a new __rtc_compatible_meta_box flag, better array attribute stability, and a WP_ALLOW_COLLABORATION kill switch. Additional quality-of-life improvements include keyboard shortcut tooltips for block movement, reordered spacing side controls, and a fix for the Separator block's --- shortcut applying the default style variation.

recent_posts.title: WordPress Core Dev Environment Toolkit: A Faster Path to Your First Core Contribution
recent_posts.summary: The WordPress Core Dev Environment Toolkit is a new desktop application for macOS, Windows, and Linux that eliminates the complex setup process for first-time WordPress core contributors. It bundles Git, Node.js, npm, and Docker equivalents as JS/WASM powered by WordPress Playground, allowing contributors to clone wordpress-develop, run a dev server, make code changes, and generate a Trac patch — all without any prerequisites or terminal work. The tool is specifically designed to solve the common Contributor Day problem where participants spend the entire session on environment setup and never actually contribute.

recent_posts.title: Matt Mullenweg calls for WordPress to re-center individual contributors over corporate sponsors
recent_posts.summary: Matt Mullenweg reflects on how the WordPress community has shifted toward over-recognizing corporate sponsors at the expense of individual contributors. He calls for a return to celebrating personal contributions, critiques badge designs that prominently display employer names over personal identity, and challenges the community to measure actual impact rather than hours pledged. He also questions how consensus-driven processes and emphasis on participation may have slowed progress, referencing The Mythical Man-Month as a long-known warning.

top_posts.title: PHP-only block registration
top_posts.summary: WordPress now supports PHP-only block registration, allowing developers to create simple blocks without any JavaScript. By calling register_block_type with the new autoRegister flag and a render_callback, blocks automatically appear in the editor. The editor also auto-generates Inspector Controls sidebar UI for supported attribute types, making it easier to build server-side-rendered blocks with minimal setup.

top_posts.title: JSX in WordPress 6.6
top_posts.summary: WordPress 6.6 introduces the new React JSX transform, providing developers with performance improvements and optimization. Build scripts need to make changes to include dependencies and use the new JSX calls. Compatible build tools and upgrade path are also discussed.

top_posts.title: Planning for 7.0
top_posts.summary: WordPress 7.0 development is underway following the 6.9 release. Core contributors are focusing on Phase 3 collaboration features, including improvements to the Notes feature with better diffing mechanics and change reconciliation. Navigation workflow simplifications are planned to make menu management more intuitive. The team is exploring streamlined editing experiences for composite blocks and design patterns, plus more intuitive page navigation in the site editor. Additional blocks and tools are being added to expand capabilities for theme builders.

top_posts.title: Coding Standard Proposal: Make it explicit that PHP files must use the .php extension
top_posts.summary: WordPress proposes standardizing PHP file extensions to only allow .php files in their coding standards. The change addresses portability and security concerns, as different web server configurations (Apache on Debian vs Fedora) handle alternative extensions like .phtml and .php3 inconsistently. Using only .php ensures universal compatibility across server environments and guarantees that code analysis tools like PHPCS will properly check all PHP files.
